subject.title: feat(plugins): add manifest-first host contribution bundles

question: Should OpenClaw permanently add `hostIntegrationBundle` as a generic versioned plugin-manifest API, or should host-specific composition remain in the owning external plugin until a shared core consumer is established?
rationale: The implementation is intentionally inert but creates a new public plugin contract whose naming, versioning, and ownership cannot be selected safely from code correctness alone.

options.title: Confirm the manifest contract
options.body: Accept this as the canonical generic inventory boundary and proceed with owner-reviewed API and documentation expectations.

options.title: Pause for a narrower boundary
options.body: Keep the composition in the external owner plugin or extend an existing generic contract only after a concrete shared consumer proves the new API is necessary.

recommendation.title: Pause for a narrower boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the composition in the external owner plugin or extend an existing generic contract only after a concrete shared consumer proves the new API is necessary.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR explicitly routes the manifest-contract decision to this owner boundary.
